heroLead: Port Washington sits along the historic Ohio and Erie Canal route in Tuscarawas County, on the flank of the Utica/Point Pleasant play, in territory where farming and canal-era commerce shaped land patterns more than oil and gas ever did.
intro: The canal-era history around Port Washington means a lot of local land was platted and divided for commerce and small farms well before anyone drilled a modern shale well nearby. That history is part of why mineral ownership records here can be older and more fragmented than in areas developed later.

sections.heading: Canal-era land division and mineral title
paragraphs: Small lots and farm tracts platted during the canal era near Port Washington were sometimes subdivided repeatedly over the following century, and mineral rights weren't always addressed consistently in each transaction. A full title check is the only reliable way to know whether your specific parcel's minerals were ever severed from the surface.

sections.heading: Tuscarawas County's flank position today
paragraphs: Modern Utica/Point Pleasant development has been more selective in Tuscarawas County than in the core counties to the east. Value on a Port Washington-area tract depends on proximity to the nearest actual units, so checking recent permit activity in the surrounding area is a practical step.

sections.heading: Recorder records in New Philadelphia
paragraphs: The Tuscarawas County Recorder's office in New Philadelphia holds deed and lease history for Port Washington. Given the area's older land-division patterns, plan to check a full chain of title rather than just the most recent deed.

faqs.question: Does Port Washington's canal history affect mineral rights?
faqs.answer: It can complicate the title trail. Land platted and subdivided during the canal era sometimes went through more transactions than typical farmland, so mineral rights weren't always addressed the same way each time.

faqs.question: Is Tuscarawas County heavily drilled?
faqs.answer: It sits on the flank of the play, with more selective development than the core counties further east. Local value depends on proximity to specific active units.

faqs.question: Where do I check my title history?
faqs.answer: The Tuscarawas County Recorder's office in New Philadelphia holds deed records for the entire county, including Port Washington.

faqs.question: Why would a canal-era deed omit mineral rights language?
faqs.answer: Deeds from that period often focused on surface use and commerce rather than subsurface rights, since deep shale drilling wasn't a consideration at the time. That's exactly why a full title check matters now.

faqs.question: Is it common for canal-era parcels to have irregular boundary descriptions?
faqs.answer: Yes, older surveys in this area sometimes used metes-and-bounds descriptions tied to landmarks that no longer exist, which can complicate matching your parcel to a modern unit boundary. A title professional can usually resolve this.
